_about: Scientific data library, domain muscular: the universal columns of the game's body/data/muscular.json tables, written by scripts/split_data.py. Same columns/rows schema as the game's tables. `id` is stable (see README); `source` holds source keys from sources.json ('; ' separated) or 'open'. Mark is the review state of these columns. A null in a column the engine's data/*.json holds by the same id means the engine file is the home of that value.

fatigue_rates.title: Three-compartment fatigue model (3CC): rates by joint
fatigue_rates.source: Xia and Frey Law 2008 (J Biomech): muscle in resting, active, fatigued compartments; F = fatigue rate active to fatigued, R = recovery rate fatigued to resting, per second. endurance_time.title: How long a hold lasts at a given effort (Rohmert-type endurance curve)
endurance_time.source: Rohmert 1960 and later fits: endurance time falls steeply with %MVC; below about 15% MVC a hold is sustainable for a long time (the ergonomic design limit). Numbers here are the keeper's reading of general curves, not one study. MUS-ROH

activations.title: Action activation profiles (% of the group's maximum; illustrative)
activations.source: Shape from EMG literature where it exists (inverted row and suspension rows: lats, mid trapezius, biceps, rear deltoid at 50 to 60% MVIC; climbing postures: middle and lower trapezius 35 to 60%; MUS-EMG). Hauling rope is ChatGPT's illustrative profile (gears/muscular-state-model.md). Every other profile is the keeper's estimate and a data task to refine. The columns are the groups by id; a blank is 0.

training.title: Training, adaptation and disuse constants
training.source: Protein 1.6 g/kg/day is the plateau for resistance-training gains (Morton et al. 2018 meta-analysis, BJSM; MUS-PROT). DOMS peaks 24 to 72 h and clears by 7 days (MUS-DOMS). Muscle protein synthesis stays raised 24 to 48 h after lifting (textbook). Supercompensation (gain after recovery) is the Banister logic applied per group. Detraining: strength holds for about 2 to 3 weeks then falls; muscle mass loss is faster than strength loss (textbook, medium). Novice gains are fast (10 to 30% strength in 8 to 12 weeks), trained gains slow.
rows: sum over groups of activation% x reps x loadFactor, loadFactor = 0 under 40% of the group's max, rising to 1.0 at 80%+

adaptation.title: The adaptation model: what lives at which level (Rex, 2026-10-29; structure from ChatGPT's notes, outside AI)
adaptation.source: Exercise physiology: hypertrophy from mechanical tension and protein accretion; mitochondrial biogenesis, capillarisation and enzyme changes from sustained aerobic demand; early strength gains largely neural (motor-unit recruitment, 4 to 8 weeks) and movement-specific; tendons remodel slowly (months) and tolerate repeated load by that remodelling (standard references: ACSM, McArdle Katch and Katch). The structure is ChatGPT's (outside AI), the keeper agreeing: two long-term states per muscle, tendons per joint, recruitment per movement pattern, three stimuli per activity. MUS-ADAPT

patterns.title: Movement patterns (neural recruitment lives here, not per muscle and not in the skill)
patterns.source: ChatGPT's point (outside AI), kept: a man gets stronger at a movement by recruiting more of the muscle he has, without more muscle and without more skill; Swordplay is technique and timing, Reflexes is response speed, neither is maximal recruitment. The pattern set is the keeper's; each activation row names its patterns. Patterns that one arm performs are tracked per side (L/R), like the muscles, so handedness, a lost hand and one-sided training matter; the trunk and leg patterns are one.

injuries.source: Strain grading I to III is clinical standard; recovery times are typical ranges (textbook). Risk factors: fatigue, cold, no warm-up, a load far above the group's development, prior injury.

limb_strength.title: How a limb's Strength is computed from its groups (proposed answer to the replace-or-compute question)
limb_strength.source: Rex left open whether muscle replaces per-limb Strength or Strength is computed from it (gears/muscular-state-model.md; ChatGPT: replaces). This table is the 'computed' reading, offered because it keeps the per-limb Strength number alive for every system that already reads it while the muscles underneath make it per limb and trainable by what you do. Weights are the keeper's.
columns: Formula (development x (1 - fatigue) x condition, per group)
rows: weighted mean of the right arm's groups' contractile x mean recruitment of the arm's patterns, scaled to the STATS 1 to 20 range (the character-sheet number); the force in a given action is the action's own: contractile x the pattern's recruitment x (1 - fatigue) x condition per required group, the weakest limiting
